title: Keyturn Roadside Assistance: Covered Callers, Abortive Callouts and the Standing Required for Dispatch
content:
**Who may call.** Whoever is with the vehicle may call, but only where the plan covers that person; a
plan that does not cover guests will not attend a guest on a trip, and the host must call on the
guest's behalf.

**An abortive callout.** A callout called off after the operator has set out carries the plan's
cancellation fee, and one where nobody is with the vehicle when the operator arrives carries the plan's
no-show fee instead; the two are never charged together.

**The standing the subscription must have.** Dispatch is only made while the subscription is in the
active state, so a suspended or lapsed subscription is told what it would cost to reinstate rather than
attended on credit.

### The abortive-callout clause in its two branches

| What happened | Fee carried |
| --- | --- |
| The callout was called off after the operator had set out | The plan's cancellation fee |
| Nobody was with the vehicle when the operator arrived | The plan's no-show fee |

The clause sets the second fee in place of the first, not alongside it: the cancellation fee and the
no-show fee are never charged together on one callout.

### The standing requirement and what evidences it

Active is the only state in which a Keyturn Roadside Assistance subscription is dispatched on. The
state recorded against the subscription the call is made under is what carries authority, and the
subscription's reference number is what ties that record to the call; the question is settled before an
operator is sent. A subscription standing suspended, and a subscription standing lapsed, are each told
what restoring cover would cost rather than attended against the allowance.
